messages.subject: Shiny ready event
parts:
I'm writing htmlwidgets with input back to shiny - ie. you can write a reactive around input$control_name - wired up using Shiny.onInputChange. 
The initial value of input$control_name is only fired if Shiny.onInputChange is delayed until document.readystage == 'complete', plus another 2s delay (via setTimeout) 
So, 2 questions: is there a Shiny 'ready' event that one can hook into via the global Shiny object - or 2: is there another way in htmlwidgets to initialise input$control_name (other than calling Shiny.onInputChange from javascript)

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Shiny ready event
parts: To answer the first question: There is in fact a JavaScript event you can register to listen for. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/js-events.html

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ready event
parts:
Are you putting the htmlwidget directly in ui.R? It's generally easier to put our fooOutput(id) in ui.R and output$id <- renderFoo(...) in server.R (assuming your widget is named "foo"), that way the widget doesn't render until Shiny renders it (by which time it clearly will be ready for Shiny.onInputChange).

Oh and also if you put the widget directly in ui.R, then it'll never be registered for binding--it's basically part of the scenery as far as Shiny is concerned, it doesn't know the difference between a widget and an <h1> unless you use something like fooOutput(id).

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ready event
parts:
Yes, that's definitely the route I'd go right now.

The docs about input bindings predate our work with htmltools::htmlDependencies. Ideally you would do something like the below. In this example I'm assuming your package name is "myselectinputpkg" and you've put select2 JS and CSS files under the path inst/lib/select2/, and your custom Shiny input binding JS file is at inst/lib/binding/select-binding.js.

By attaching these dependencies to your UI object, you can avoid what ShinySky had to do, with "includeSelect2".

mySelectInput <- function(id, ...) {
  ui <- ... # whatever goes into your widget, i.e. div(id=id, class="myselectinput, ...)

  htmltools::attachDependencies(
    ui,
    list(
      htmltools::htmlDependency(
        "select2", "4.0.1",
        src = system.file("lib/select2", package="myselectinputpkg"),
        script = "select2.js",
        stylesheet = "select2.css"
      ),
      htmltools::htmlDependency(
        "select2-binding", packageVersion("myselectinputpkg"),
        src = system.file("lib/binding", package="myselectinputpkg"),
        script = "select-binding.js"
      )
    )
  )
}
